Chunking and Retrieval

A vector store indexes chunks of text so that a query can find the passages most similar to it. Cosine similarity is used to rank candidates, and only the top few results are returned.

Retrieval quality depends heavily on chunk size. Chunks that are too large dilute the embedding with irrelevant content; chunks that are too small lose surrounding context.
